title: Fix Sticky Navigation Bar on Scroll by Eliminating Parent Containment Wrapper
description: Fix navigation bar disappearing upon page scroll: (1) Diagnosed root cause in `components/navigation/site-header.tsx`, where `<header className="sticky top-0 ...">` was wrapped within `<div className="w-full relative z-50">`. According to CSS specification, position: sticky is constrained by the height of its containing block. Because the wrapper div had a height equal only to the announcement bar + header (~100px) and ended right above `<main>`, scrolling past 100px caused the entire wrapper to scroll out of view, taking the sticky header with it. (2) Refactored `components/navigation/site-header.tsx` to return a React Fragment `<> ... </>` containing `{showAnnouncement && <AnnouncementBar />}` and `<header className="sticky top-0 z-50 w-full backdrop-blur-md bg-[var(--background)]/90 border-b border-[var(--color-border-subtle)] transition-colors duration-200 relative">`, making `<div className="min-h-screen flex flex-col">` its containing block spanning the full page height. (3) Retained relative positioning on header so `MegaMenu`'s `absolute top-full left-0` aligns beneath it. (4) Updated `tests/navigation.spec.ts` with comprehensive scroll tests (desktop 800px scroll, y=0 bounding box verification, mega menu hover while scrolled, mobile 390x844 600px scroll with mobile nav drawer), verified build, and captured verification screenshots in both Dark and Light modes.
acceptanceCriteria: Navigation bar remains firmly pinned to top: 0 of the viewport across the entire scroll depth of the page
Announcement bar scrolls off naturally when scrolling down, and becomes visible again when scrolling back to the top
Brand wordmark, quick search button, and cart button remain fully visible, accessible, and interactable while scrolled
India Circus-inspired MegaMenu opens directly below the sticky header when hovering over 'Custom Framing' while scrolled
Mobile navigation drawer operates cleanly from the sticky hamburger button at 390x844 viewport when scrolled 600px
Sticky header adapts seamlessly across Dark Mode (#1A1A1A/90 with blur) and Light Mode (#FAF8F5/90 with blur)
All Playwright tests pass (36/36) with zero regressions
Screenshots captured while scrolled in both Dark and Light modes and saved to artifact directory and .agent/screenshots/

steps.description: Identify containing block issue in components/navigation/site-header.tsx
steps.details: Identified that `<div className="w-full relative z-50">` bounded `<header className="sticky top-0 ...">`, restricting sticky containment to ~100px height.

steps.description: Refactor site-header.tsx to eliminate wrapper div and return React Fragment
steps.details: Replaced wrapper div with `<>` fragment, added `w-full` and `relative` directly to `<header>` to preserve MegaMenu positioning.

steps.description: Implement Playwright scroll verification tests in tests/navigation.spec.ts
steps.details: Added tests verifying desktop scroll (800px, bounding box y = 0, interactive header controls, mega menu positioning) and mobile scroll (390x844, 600px, mobile drawer). Captured verification screenshots for dark and light modes.

steps.description: Execute Playwright test suite and Next.js production build
steps.details: Executed full Playwright test suite (36/36 passing) and verified clean Next.js build with zero TypeScript errors.
